newsitem.title: UK: S&P says Sweden economy has improved since Jan '95.
newsitem.headline: S&P says Sweden economy has improved since Jan '95.

text.p: The Swedish economy has improved solidly since a negative outlook was assigned to the county's sovereign debt rating by Standard and Poor's in January 1995, S&P director Konrad Reuss said on Tuesday.
Speaking at a conference in London, Reuss said the positive developments meant that "as time progresses the likelihood of a change in the outlook from negative to stable will increase."
S&P currently rates Sweden's foreign currency sovereign debt at AA plus long-term, with a negative outlook.
"Since we assigned the negative outlook to the rating (in January 1995) Sweden has shown a fairly solid performance," Reuss told the conference. "That is certainly a positive."
But he said the current negative outlook was still important to maintain because it gave a proper signal to financial markets.

He said the outlook was assigned as negative because the Swedish government was, and still is, running the risk that some kind of external event could spark "premature slippage in Sweden's fiscal adjustment programme".
